translations.24533db3073f71ee72867063: ⟪P0⟫Tested⟪P1⟫each trigger went through a test before turning on.
translations.8a473f2e32caee4c2ff38f06: ✓ Write triggers the agent recognizes by facts, and test at least the first one before turning it on.
translations.ccdb994893ba1f9d227032f4: ✗ Use vague triggers like “delicate situation,” that the agent can’t identify.
translations.3a4c0f1ba924305f5ff5580d: Write three triggers for an assistant that makes the first round of corrections to a teacher’s essays.
translations.6ddab8acab158ced228c1800: Good examples: suspected plagiarism or text made by AI, concerning content like bullying or a risk to the student, and writing that’s off-topic. All three require human judgment and have consequences for the student; the agent flags and stops, it doesn’t decide.
translations.5f82544355887a809341b608: The ritual: 2 minutes a day, 10 per week, 1 review per month
translations.a19986e34edb83bf615f173a: The ritual goes from most frequent and short to rare and strategic, and each frequency has a different question.
translations.e600a8fb8e6df1099d046aa2: ⟪P0⟫Before turning on⟪P1⟫3 tests, updated source, team informed.
translations.af5a90dd6ce6eae4260900a3: ⟪P0⟫Every day⟪P1⟫2 minutes in the report and past cases.
translations.291176a8cf978b9b5fb23e12: ⟪P0⟫Every week⟪P1⟫10 minutes and an adjusted rule.
translations.cf3ded2f1fe43ba40b98d650: ⟪P0⟫Every month⟪P1⟫is the level and the task still the right ones?
translations.80fa75bb46d0164b5d12f52c: ✓ Mark on your calendar the report time and the day of the weekly review, as a fixed commitment.
translations.7d7956b9b7e0b3c74cc59778: ✗ Change multiple rules at the same time after a bad week.
translations.d8a03bd4c2605bdcba9510c3: Pick an agent of yours and set the exact time for the daily report and the day of the weekly review.
translations.014c7cd5ce13a18ad9eeb798: The best time is right after the agent finishes its shift, when you can still act on the same day. The weekly review works best on a calm day, like Friday morning or early Monday. If you can’t name the time, supervision doesn’t exist yet.
translations.6f8ec7662b2b029ec1611750: The agent sits in the middle of the process, but the ends—defining and responding—stay human.
translations.e29d5f3883cb3a81c5e1bfbb: ⟪P0⟫Judgment⟪P1⟫on exceptions, new cases, and dilemmas stays with you.
translations.9c6fe75517bd6fddd0462eff: ⟪P0⟫Auditing⟪P1⟫checking by sample, even when the report is clean.
translations.1d293754da924f9e2e826467: ⟪P0⟫Limits⟪P1⟫only you raise the level or remove a prohibition.
translations.a844f1b759c6a013d1f4fabb: Objectives and limits: identifying the initial condition.
translations.73bdbbb5f09388046e8dfd02: Agent executes: applying the described decision.
translations.c96619e6f123248712d243a7: You audit and decide on exceptions: check the effect in the example.
translations.07c4a12117b6c4ef3202d0ea: You are responsible for the outcome: record the output evidence.
translations.0e3fbf562c113a8fc466e347: ✓ Check a sample of the work every week, even when the report says everything is fine.
translations.27986d89aa55f60e3864903d: ✗ Let the agent decide exceptions because it “already knows the client.”
translations.0accc09b9995e4f4cbdfb581: List two decisions from your business that you would never hand to an agent, even at N4, and explain why.
translations.e86c1104f0a1cde8dfd95a54: Typical examples: approving a commercial exception for a client and responding to a formal complaint. Both require context, empathy, and responsibility that you can’t transfer. The agent can prepare the information, but the decision and signature are yours.
translations.e5ec6c53ff93a9203f454c5b: The cycle: error becomes a rule
translations.6b0118d3af83e7114274b820: Each turn of the cycle transforms an error into a rule, and the sum of the turns is what justifies moving up a level.
translations.b0a7ea26574ac51cd42f1794: ⟪P0⟫Executes⟪P1⟫the agent works within the agreed level.
translations.ada972f02d12e6cc51695628: ⟪P0⟫Observes⟪P1⟫report and failure log show what happened.
